layers.title: Foreign-born stock by corridor
layers.question: How many people born in one country are living in another?
layers.note: Modelled, not counted. These are the migrant-stock estimates the flow model is fitted against, and they reach a year further than the flows do because the flow for a year is inferred from the change between two stock anchors. A stock is a standing population, not a movement: do not read a change between two anchors as a flow, and never sum stocks across years. This layer ships the 9,200 largest of 53,130 corridors — the top 25 on each side of every country — which is 97.6% of the estimated stock. The two country layers are summed over all of them and are not trimmed.

layers.title: Foreign-born population
layers.question: How many people living here were born somewhere else?
layers.note: Modelled, not counted. These are the migrant-stock estimates the flow model is fitted against, and they reach a year further than the flows do because the flow for a year is inferred from the change between two stock anchors. Summed over every origin, so it is the destination margin of the corridor layer rather than an independent measurement of it.

layers.title: People born here living abroad
layers.question: How many people born in this country are living somewhere else?
layers.note: Modelled, not counted. These are the migrant-stock estimates the flow model is fitted against, and they reach a year further than the flows do because the flow for a year is inferred from the change between two stock anchors. The origin margin of the same matrix. A country can be large on this layer and small on the foreign-born layer, or both at once.
